sources.title: Connect Multiple DGX Spark through a Switch (dgx-spark-playbooks)

open_questions: None of the connect-two/three/switch/NCCL playbooks publish actual measured bandwidth (GB/s) or NCCL all_gather results for DGX Spark despite running the tests -- only the 200Gbps link-speed target is documented. Need to run these tests ourselves on NvidiaSpark-1 (+ a second unit, if/when acquired) to get real numbers for ch22.

No official NVIDIA multi-node inference tok/s or context-length numbers exist for DGX Spark clusters (NCCL playbook explicitly stops at 'next step: TRT-LLM or vLLM' without providing figures) -- ch6/ch22 concurrency claims will need empirical validation on our own hardware.

NeMo fine-tune playbook claims '1-70B parameter' support on DGX Spark but gives zero GPU memory, time, or loss numbers -- the 70B QLoRA-on-128GB-unified-memory claim is unverified by NVIDIA's own doc and should be tested directly.

None of the RAPIDS/cuDF/cuML/cuOpt data-science playbooks (cuda-x-data-science, portfolio-optimization) mention Apache Spark or the RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark at all -- the ch18 CDP-on-AWS/RAPIDS-Accelerator-for-Spark integration story is not covered by any official DGX Spark playbook and needs separate research (Cloudera docs / RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark project) outside this bucket's source set.

cuTile Kernels playbook's Qwen2-7B 18.52 tok/s figure is presumably single-stream/single-request -- unclear if this represents batch=1 or a specific concurrency level; worth confirming before quoting in ch6.

load_bearing_claims.claim: LLaMA Factory playbook: measured LoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-4B on DGX Spark completed in ~14m32s at 3.749 samples/sec, loss 0.9993 after 3 epochs, 11,076,559 GF total FLOPs -- the only playbook in this bucket with real measured fine-tune numbers.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: This is the single concrete, NVIDIA-published fine-tune performance data point for DGX Spark in the whole playbooks set; ch6/ch22 should cite this rather than the unmeasured NeMo/PyTorch/Unsloth playbooks, and set expectations that other playbooks' claims (e.g. 70B on 128GB) are unverified until we test them ourselves.

load_bearing_claims.claim: cuTile Kernels playbook: DGX Spark end-to-end Qwen2-7B inference measured at 18.52 tokens/sec, vs B300's 257.33 tokens/sec (13.9x faster).
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Rare official DGX-Spark-specific tok/s number, useful for setting realistic single-GPU expectations in ch6 (perf/concurrency chapter) -- shows DGX Spark is a dev/prototyping box, not a production-throughput inference box, relative to B300.

load_bearing_claims.claim: None of NVIDIA's official DGX Spark playbooks (CUDA-X Data Science, Portfolio Optimization, or any other) mention Apache Spark or the RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark -- they only use standalone cuDF/cuML/cuOpt.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Directly affects ch18's premise: there is no NVIDIA-validated DGX-Spark + Apache-Spark/RAPIDS-Accelerator integration path documented anywhere in this playbook repo; the CDP Base on AWS RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark story must be built/validated independently, not copied from an existing playbook.

load_bearing_claims.claim: Unsloth playbook's '2x faster / up to 30x multi-GPU' speedup claim is Unsloth's own generic marketing figure carried into the NVIDIA doc verbatim, explicitly NOT a DGX-Spark-measured benchmark.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: This number is likely to circulate in X posts/community discussion as if it were DGX-Spark-specific; the guide must not cite it as hardware-measured data without a caveat.
